title: Batch usage shipper: scheduled CSV/S3 exports + webhook notifications
creator: Arjun Patel
description: Build a backend service to produce scheduled customer usage exports (CSV as primary, optional Parquet), deliverable to customer S3 buckets or Redwood-managed S3 via presigned URLs, with optional webhook notifications on completion/failure. Exports must support hourly/daily/weekly schedules, incremental cursors for large tenants, column-schema versioning, RBAC controls in Console, and audit logging for compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Customers can create scheduled exports from Console with destination: external S3, Redwood S3, or webhook
Exports support CSV by default; Parquet option available for large exports
Exports are incremental when possible (cursor) and support full historical backfill
Presigned upload + server-side encryption used for external S3 uploads; secrets are never stored in plaintext
Webhook payloads include export metadata and a signed delivery token; retries/exponential backoff implemented
RBAC: only org admins or roles with 'exports:manage' can create/update/delete scheduled exports
Export audit entries written to audit-log service and visible in Console export history
Performance: daily export for 1k-10k orgs completes within 2 hours; large orgs (>100k requests/day) use chunked exports and background re-tries
design_decisions: CSV chosen as default for compatibility with customer BI tools; Parquet offered to reduce size and speed (opt-in)
Airflow will orchestrate export DAGs querying materialized hourly aggregates in Redshift. We considered streaming direct queries from OLTP but rejected for cost and contention reasons
Use a dedicated 'export-scheduler' service that owns scheduling metadata and triggers Airflow DAGs via REST API instead of embedding schedule logic in Airflow to keep lifecycle decoupled
Delivery methods: prefer customer-managed S3 via presigned PUT URLs for scalability and security. For webhook delivery, deliver a signed JSON manifest with presigned download URLs for artifacts
Keep exports immutable after creation; updates create a new export run. This simplifies retry and audit models
Incremental exports use a monotonic 'export_cursor' stored per org in exports DB table; cursor is based on materialized-aggregate window ID to avoid missing events when aggregates are reprocessed
implementation_plan: Schema: add exports table (id, org_id, schedule_cron, destination_type, destination_config_id, format, last_cursor, status, created_by, created_at)
API: Console backend endpoints: POST /v1/orgs/:id/exports, GET /v1/orgs/:id/exports, POST /v1/exports/:id/trigger, DELETE /v1/exports/:id
Scheduler: new export-scheduler service (K8s Deployment) subscribes to exports DB changes and enqueues runs to Airflow via REST, or triggers immediate runs for one-offs
Airflow DAG: export_run_{format} reads last_cursor -> queries materialized aggregates -> writes CSV/Parquet to S3 prefix -> updates export_run table and exports.last_cursor
Delivery: generate presigned S3 PUT for customer buckets (validate bucket policies & restrict to prefix). For Redwood-managed bucket, write directly with SSE-KMS using per-org KMS keys

Webhook: after write, call customer webhook with signed payload; implement at-most-once semantics via idempotency keys and retries using exponential backoff + dead-letter queue (SNS->Lambda for small fanouts considered)
Auth/Permissions: integrate with existing RBAC service; require org-level permission checks and logging
Monitoring: metrics (runs_started, runs_succeeded, bytes_written, avg_runtime) + alerts for run failures >3 consecutive
Testing: unit tests for scheduler, integration tests that run DAGs against a test Redshift dataset, and e2e smoke test delivering to sandbox S3 and webhook endpoints
work_items: ENG-4853: schema migration for exports and export_runs tables
ENG-4854: build export-scheduler service skeleton + DB watcher
ENG-4855: Airflow DAG to generate CSV and Parquet using Redshift materialized views
ENG-4856: presigned S3 flow + validation + KMS integration
ENG-4857: webhook delivery worker with retry/DLQ
ENG-4858: Console UI integration + API endpoints
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Large exports can monopolize Redshift cluster. Mitigation: rate-limit concurrent export runs per cluster and queue large jobs to low-priority workers; offer Parquet + compression to reduce IO
Risk: Presigned URL misuse or wrong bucket. Mitigation: validate bucket ownership via S3:GetBucketPolicy or require customer to add verification token; set short TTL on presigned URLs
Risk: Webhook endpoints of customers can be slow/failure-prone. Mitigation: make webhook delivery async with retries and DLQ; allow customers to opt-in to webhook vs. S3
Risk: Schema drift breaks downstream BI. Mitigation: include schema_version in export manifest and keep v1 CSV compatibility for 6 months; include header rows and column descriptions
